title: Late Miocene expansion of C4 grasslands
summary: In the Siwalik deposits of northern Pakistan, soil carbon isotopes show C3 vegetation giving way to C4 grasses from about 7.3 million years ago, with floodplain vegetation close to pure C4 grassland by about 6 Ma. A study of Siwalik and Bengal Fan sediments finds a relatively rapid shift in plant-wax carbon isotopes before 6 Ma, with soil changes possibly beginning as early as 9 Ma.

uncertainty.note: Range runs from the earliest suggested onset ("as early as 9 Ma", Freeman and Colarusso 2001) to near-pure C4 grassland at about 6 Ma (Quade and Cerling 1995), whose own onset is 7.3 Ma. The id uses 8 Ma. Years are Ma with no 1950 offset.

as_recorded.value: At 7.3 Ma, a shift toward more positive carbon isotopic values began

when.display: c. 9–6 million years ago (onset 7.3 Ma in northern Pakistan)

where.modern_name: Potwar Plateau, northern Pakistan (Siwalik sections; the Indian subcontinent record is wider)
where.historical_name: Northern Indian subcontinent, Late Miocene; no polities

importance.justification: A major shift in terrestrial vegetation recorded in Siwalik isotopes.
